name: Carnelian-Vast
description: Carnelian-Vast dominates its system like a burning eye, its atmosphere banded in deep reds, oranges, and the warm brown of polished carnelian stone. A planet-spanning hurricane larger than most terrestrial worlds churns in the southern hemisphere, its eye a vortex of descending golden gas that has persisted for recorded centuries. Magnetic anomalies at both poles generate aurora displays visible from neighboring planets.

Approaching Carnelian-Vast is an exercise in humility. The cloud bands scroll past with deceptive slowness, each one a weather system thousands of kilometers wide, moving at speeds that would flatten any structure built by human hands. The dense atmosphere roars with electrical discharge, a constant bombardment of static that fills every radio frequency with noise.

An orbital station of unknown manufacture drifts in a stable Lagrange point, its design matching no known architectural tradition. It appears to have been a gas-harvesting platform, its collection scoops extended into the upper atmosphere on cables of extraordinary tensile strength. The station is powered down but structurally intact, and preliminary surveys suggest it was abandoned rather than destroyed.

Carnelian-Vast's helium-3 reserves are among the richest in the sector, making the derelict station a prize worth claiming for whoever can restart its systems. Multiple salvage teams have attempted boarding operations, but the station's internal layout is disorienting and several teams have reported equipment malfunctions with no clear cause. The gas giant keeps its secrets behind walls of wind and static.
